name: tabular_recsys_leaky
title: The recommender's defective twin: negatives drawn from the whole table, an unguarded evaluation pass and a tensor-valued running loss
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-tabular: the defective half of the recommender pair

expected.defect: the training loader is constructed at module scope with num_workers=4 and the module has no __main__ guard
expected.why: on macOS and Windows each worker re-imports the module, which re-runs build_datasets and the print at the bottom

expected.defect: the evaluation loader has the same defect on the next statement
expected.why: same spawn semantics; both loaders are built before any function is called
the hit-rate is computed per batch, so the rows it averages over change between runs and the number is not reproducible

expected.defect: the evaluation pass never calls model.eval()
expected.why: the module stays in training mode, so any dropout or batch-norm layer added later silently corrupts the metric

expected.defect: the evaluation loop is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: the whole holdout is materialised as autograd history that is never used, which is the usual cause of an out-of-memory at evaluation time

expected.defect: the running loss accumulates the loss tensor rather than loss.item()
expected.why: every batch's autograd graph stays alive for the whole epoch, so memory grows linearly with the number of batches

expected.defect: nothing seeds torch, numpy or random, and the negative sampler draws from np.random
expected.why: two runs disagree on both the embeddings and the negatives they were trained against

unsupported.shape: a negative sampler built from the full interaction table
unsupported.wouldBe: no catalogued rule; it is the recommender-domain instance of MLV101, with the 'transformer' being a hand-written class rather than a scikit-learn one
unsupported.why: an item the user buys after the cut is excluded from the negative pool, which is exactly the information the hit-rate is supposed to measure

forbidden.why: the training loader passes shuffle=True at line 31
backward() at line 43 comes before step() at line 44
there is no no_grad block in this file at all, so no backward can be inside one
no device is ever named in this project - the model and the batches are both on the default device
there is no .cuda() call and no 'cuda' literal anywhere
both submodules are plain attributes, which nn.Module registers
nothing is saved or loaded in this project
the holdout is a timestamp quantile; train_test_split and random_split never appear
